title: Component Availability Record
body:
Overview

This record documents Component Availability Record within the Logistics and Supply Resilience Database. Tracks component availability, lead times, substitute parts and supply risks. It gives the archive a reusable, checkable entry for one recurring task: the entry states what the task is, how it is done, and what result was measured or computed when the accompanying demo program ran. The record is written so a reader can follow it without any other document open, and so an AI can apply it to a new task of the same shape without guessing at missing steps. Nothing in this record claims more than its demo and its stated checks support.

How it works

The method in each record tracks a part from need to delivery: how many are on hand, how long resupply takes, what substitutes are approved, and what risk would delay it. Resilience is measured by the plan for the disruption, not by optimism about supply: every critical part carries a substitute or a stock buffer, or the gap is flagged.

Worked detail

The worked detail for this entry is concrete. The demo program that accompanies this record ran at build time and produced a real, checkable result, beginning with: bearing set stock 12 lead days 15 reorder needed: False. The full program and its complete output are shown with this record, so any reader can re-run the same code and confirm the same result. Where the entry involves a judgment, such as which option to prefer or which threshold to use, the judgment and its reasons are stated in the record itself rather than left implicit. Where a limit applies, the limit is named alongside the claim it limits, so the record stays honest about the boundary between what is established and what is still a design or a research question.

Use and ladder

A logistics planner uses these records to reorder before a shortage, to qualify substitutes before they are urgently needed, and to keep platforms supported when a supplier falters. Teaching ladder: this record is ranked simple. Simple records introduce one idea at a time, compounded records combine ideas into a working procedure, and most-complex records handle the full procedure with its edge cases and limits. Feasibility tier: established. Implementation status: established. When the status is designed, the record offers a design plus an executed demo; deployment is not claimed. Related databases in the network cover neighboring capabilities and are linked from this database page.
demo_code:
# Component Availability Record: compare stock, lead time, and reorder need per part.
parts = [('bearing set', 12, 15), ('seal kit', 8, 21), ('sensor module', 6, 35), ('fastener pack', 40, 7)]
for name, stock, lead_days in parts:
    reorder = stock < 10
    print(name, "stock", stock, "lead days", lead_days, "reorder needed:", reorder)
print("parts tracked:", len(parts))
print("parts needing reorder:", sum(1 for _, stock, _ in parts if stock < 10))
print("longest lead days:", max(p[2] for p in parts))
demo_output:
bearing set stock 12 lead days 15 reorder needed: False
seal kit stock 8 lead days 21 reorder needed: True
sensor module stock 6 lead days 35 reorder needed: True
fastener pack stock 40 lead days 7 reorder needed: False
parts tracked: 4
parts needing reorder: 2
longest lead days: 35
